blocks.text:
I need to find the worst steric clash between two residues, likely in side chains given it's a 89-residue single chain. I'm checking the MSE13 selenium and carbon positions against nearby residues like LEU9 to spot unusually short contacts.

Continuing to check distances around other MSE residues, comparing their side chain atoms against nearby leucine and aspartate residues, but most pairs remain too far apart to count as clashes.

I'm now stepping back to look at the overall fold by tracing CA positions along the chain at intervals of five residues, trying to map out the helical hairpin structure and identify which segments run close enough to each other to plausibly clash.

Checking residues around positions 9, 13, and 55-56, I'm measuring side-chain distances between MSE13, LEU9, and VAL55/PHE56 to see if any atom pairs come close enough to count as a steric clash.

Now I'm comparing helix packing between residues 20-31 and looking at LEU21/PHE31, then LEU37/LEU57 pairs, checking CB-CB distances to identify which specific side-chain pair produces the tightest, most likely clashing contact in the structure.

I'm pulling together the full list of CA coordinates for all residues to systematically scan for the closest non-sequential pairs before diving into atom-level distance checks.

Continuing through the remaining coordinates, I spot a couple residue numbering ambiguities to double check, then start scanning for non-adjacent CA pairs that come unusually close together, which would hint at tertiary contacts or a compact fold—checking distances like residue 6 to 9 to see if they fall within a tight threshold.

Still not finding an obvious steric clash checking these pairs—33/57, 30/61, 26/65 all come out a bit too far apart. The tightest so far is ALA30/ALA61 side chains at ~5.3Å. Maybe I should look more carefully at the turn regions around 44-48 and 24-26, or reconsider whether the clash involves side chains rather than backbone atoms—checking HIS45 against VAL44 next.

Now I'm checking HIS43's imidazole ring against GLU40's carboxylate, finding they're about 4.0Å apart—still not quite a clash. I'm also tracing LYS3's long flexible side chain down to its NZ atom at z=-13.7, wondering if it reaches close enough to residues near HIS45/VAL44 to cause a clash, though nothing definitive yet.

I then pivot to SER47, measuring its CA, CB, and N positions against LYS3's CE atom, getting distances around 4.4-4.5Å—close but not clashing. I rule out HIS2 as too far from the helix region, then shift to checking PHE71's aromatic ring coordinates against nearby SER67, GLU70, and SER78 side chains, none of which appear close enough to matter.

I move on to ILE77's side chain atoms, comparing them against ARG76, LYS79, and ARG80, finding the closest distance around 5.6Å to ARG80's CB—still not a real clash. Considering the possibility that the actual steric conflict involves an i, i+4 pairing of bulky side chains within a helix, I compare PHE20 and PHE23's ring positions, finding them too distant, then check PHE23's ring atoms against GLN19's side chain, with distances still exceeding 4.5Å.

Next I check GLN12's side chain against ASN15 and find them too far apart, then look at GLU8's side chain relative to GLU5, ASP4, and LEU7 without finding anything close enough either. I start rechecking backbone atoms between residues 10 and 55, and begin comparing MSE13's atoms against VAL55 in more detail.

Working through the distance between MSE13's CG and VAL55's CG1 gives about 4.46 Å, still not tight enough. I keep scanning nearby side chains — VAL55 against LEU9, LEU58 against VAL55 and MSE13's CE — but each pairing comes back too far apart, so I continue checking LEU58's CD2 against other residues like ALA54, LEU62, and now ALA61.

I shift to scanning helix residues for close contacts, checking LEU7's CD1/CD2 against LYS3's CG and CD, getting distances around 4.25 and 4.87 which are still borderline loose. Then I look at LEU6's side chain against HIS10, LEU9, and MSE1's CE — the MSE1 CE to LEU6 CD1 distance comes out to about 3.67 Å, which sits right at the edge of acceptable van der Waals contact for two carbons, so I want to check the CE to CD2 distance too.

I'm now considering that the clash might just be a natural feature of a real structure rather than something artificial, so I'm scanning lysine side chains for close contacts. Checking LYS3's NZ and CE atoms against nearby VAL44 and HIS45 backbone atoms, most distances come out around 3-4Å, which is fine, but LYS3 NZ to LYS46's backbone oxygen comes out to about 2.59Å—close enough to look like a hydrogen bond rather than a clash.

I keep sweeping through other lysines—LYS17, LYS46, LYS48, LYS52, LYS79—checking their NZ positions against nearby side chains like HIS43, LEU21, PHE31, and ASP27, but most distances are too far to register as real contacts. I'm now moving on to check ARG76's side chain geometry for potential clashes.

Nothing there lines up either—ARG76's guanidinium and ARG80's NH atoms don't sit close enough to SER72, ILE77, or PHE71 to matter. I'm broadening the search to look for possible carboxylate-carboxylate clashes between ASP and GLU residues, and also checking hydrophobic packing between ILE16, LEU62, and PHE20 in case a buried side chain pair is causing the steric overlap.

Nothing between VAL26, HIS25, ASP27, or ALA33/LEU57/HIS53 is close enough either, so I'm now checking TYR34's ring and hydroxyl against nearby GLU40, LEU37, ALA54, and PHE31 side chains, then moving to VAL39.

Still finding everything a bit too far apart — VAL39's side chain, GLU50's carboxylate, and LYS46 all come in around 3.3-3.7 Å, close but not clashing. I'm not finding anything under 3 Å yet, so I'll shift focus to the region around residues 44-48 where helix 2 ends and a turn begins.

Checking HIS51's imidazole ring against LYS3 and VAL39 turns up nothing closer than 4 Å. I'm also scanning PRO41's ring against GLU11, HIS43, and LEU7, but those distances stay well above threshold too. Next I want to work through residues 54-58 against the 9-13 helix region more thoroughly, starting with ALA54's beta carbon position.

Switching to the 82-89 loop, I find GLU83's side chain oxygen (OE1) sitting only about 2.06 Å from LYS79's NZ nitrogen—that's a real clash, and it looks like it could actually be a salt bridge rather than a steric problem.

I'm scanning through other charged residue pairs across the structure—arginines, lysines, glutamates, aspartates, histidines—checking their distances to see if any potential salt bridges or clashes come closer than the 2.06 Å LYS79-GLU83 contact I found. So far nothing else stands out as shorter.

I'm also checking hydroxyl-bearing serines and threonines against nearby carboxylates for possible hydrogen bonds, finding a few borderline contacts around 2.8–3.3 Å with THR29 and SER47, but nothing unusually tight.

The 2.06 Å N–O distance still looks like the closest contact so far. To be thorough, I'm now trying to reorganize the structure by helix segments (roughly residues 1-24, 25-45, 46-70) based on their CA coordinates and trace how each helix axis runs through space relative to the others, checking for any close backbone or sidechain approaches I might have missed between helices.

Checking the helix A/helix C interface specifically, I'm measuring distances between sidechain atoms of residues like LEU9, VAL55, and PHE56, but these all come out well beyond typical clash distances (4+ Å), so nothing concerning there.

Moving to ILE16, MSE13, and LYS17, I'm running similar pairwise distance checks against LEU58, LEU62, ALA61, and GLY59 — again all distances land in the 3.7-5+ Å range, so no problematic contacts on that side either. Now I'm checking whether LYS17's side chain, which points away from helix C, instead makes contact with PHE31 on helix B.

I find LYS17's CD and CG atoms sit around 3.7-4.8 Å from PHE31's ring atoms, and PHE31's ring in turn shows some closer approaches to LEU58's CD2 (~3.9 Å), suggesting a modest but acceptable packing interaction there. Shifting to the helix B/C interface, I'm now comparing residues 34, 37, 38, 41 against 46, 50, 51, 54 — LEU37's CD2 comes close to ALA54's CB at about 3.66 Å, which is a slight but tolerable proximity, while its other contacts with HIS51, GLU50, and HIS53 stay comfortably distant. I'm continuing to work through VAL39, GLU40, and PRO41 distances next.

Moving to PHE71, I'm checking its ring atoms against nearby residues 67, 68, and 75, finding it's largely solvent-exposed with no close clashes. I then turn to helix D (residues 76-89), examining internal packing among MSE81, ILE77, LEU84, ALA85, and ALA88 — these all appear well-separated with no problematic contacts, and I'm now tracing through the 73-77 region's side chain positions including SER73, ALA74, ARG76, and ILE77 to check for any tight packing there.

After exhaustively checking surrounding regions — GLU70, LYS79, ARG76, ASP86, GLU82, GLU83's oxygen atoms, and numerous other residue pairs across helices A through D, plus regions around residues 1-25, 33-48, and 52-89 — I find none of these come close to a severe clash. The LYS79 NZ to GLU83 OE1 distance holds up as the standout at 2.06 Å, confirming this pairing as the most severe overlap in the structure: A:K79--A:E83.
